Also, note correction of premise: "Repeatable Read ... should make combined decisions equivalent to serial execution" — false; documented that RR prevents phantom reads in PG (stronger than standard minimum, which allows phantoms), but RR permits serialization anomalies; applevel-consistency says integrity checks can fail due to read/write conflicts; attempts to enforce business rules at RR are not likely to work without explicit locks. Also to enforce cross-row invariant: use Serializable, or explicit locks (SELECT FOR UPDATE / LOCK TABLE) acquired before queries in RR.

Recovery premise: retry only the failed statement — wrong. Docs: retry complete transaction including logic deciding which SQL/values; PostgreSQL offers no automatic retry. Also on error, transaction is aborted; in RR, "could not serialize access due to concurrent update" rolls back the transaction. After a serialization failure in PostgreSQL, the transaction is aborted and must be rolled back; the failed statement retry inside the same aborted transaction will fail with "current transaction is aborted". Can I cite that? The transaction-iso page says "the repeatable read transaction will be rolled back" and "abort the current transaction and retry the whole transaction from the beginning." The serialization failure page says "It is important to retry the complete transaction." Good enough. Maybe I could cite sql-rollback or "current transaction is aborted" from the error message — not necessary.

Unique violations: docs say in some cases appropriate to retry 23505 and 23P01, but more care is needed since they might be persistent conditions; do not retry unconditionally. So the generic wrapper that retries every unique violation without inspecting cause is wrong.

Three-attempt promise: docs explicitly say completion may take many attempts, and with a conflicting prepared transaction it may be impossible until it commits/rolls back; no upper bound promise possible. Mark as unsupported guarantee.

Who owns retrying: the application (client), since PostgreSQL offers no automatic retry facility. Retry unit: entire transaction, including decision logic and re-reading. Serializable + app retry is the recommended narrow change: set default_transaction_isolation = serializable, ensure no other levels used (trigger checks), retry on 40001 unconditionally; maybe also 40P01 (deadlock).

So absence of phantoms doesn't equal serial equivalence — serialization anomaly is the relevant prohibited phenomenon at Serializable only. Cite transaction-iso Table 13.1 and RR subsection.
